question: A, B, C, D, E and F live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it, number 2 and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6. The product of floors on which F and E live is 15. C lives immediately above B. The sum of floors on which D and E live is 7. How many people live between B and D?
solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, E and F live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it, number 2 and so on till the topmost floor is numbered 6.

1) The product of floors on which F and E live is 15.

Possible pairs of floor numbers whose product is 15 are (3, 5) or (5, 3).

So, F and E live on floors 3 and 5, or 5 and 3.
